learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental knowledge about flexible manufacturing, numerical control, and automation of machining processes.
Develop applied competencies in CNC programming, industrial process analysis, and optimization of manufacturing operations.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, establishing goals and meeting objectives.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the discipline's own conventions.
Effectively apply techniques related to bibliographic search and the use of reliable data sources or other information systems.

syllabus_topics: The computer in the production cycle
Programming concepts in CNC machine tools
teaching_methods: Participative lecture, conferences, company visits, fair attendance (Expositive class)
Individual or group case resolution, role-playing, application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates (Participative class)
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment; research sessions on classroom didactics (Laboratory)
Personalized attention and small group instruction to review/redirect class materials, learning, and task completion; specific student queries; programmed tutorials (Tutorial)
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects for submission and presentation in practical classes (Group work)
Student study: preparation of readings, exams, exercises, class preparation (Individual work)
assessment_rules: The final grade (N_F) is calculated as 0.5 * Written Exam Grade (N_PE) + 0.5 * Practical Test Grade (N_PO). To pass, N_F must be equal to or greater than 5 points, and N_PE must not be less than 4 points. If N_PE is below 4 points, the course is considered failed, and the final grade will be capped below 4 points. In the second call, the grade for the written exam component can be retaken, while the grades for other parts are respected.
